solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legendary captain, a pilot with KLM?

definitions.meaning: the master of the ghost ship of sea legend, doomed to sail forever
KLM is the Dutch national airline, so one of its pilots is an airborne Netherlander

explanation.surface: A question whether some famous seafaring hero of legend flew for the Dutch airline.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a pilot for the Dutch airline is literally a Dutchman who flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phantom ship's captain of folklore is known by this name, as is the ship itself.

clue.text: Labour leader eg takes holidays with Balls?

indicators.note: the leader of the word Labour is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
short holidays are breaks

explanation.surface: A Labour leader taking holidays with Ed Balls, the Labour politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks like the surname of Ed Balls, a Labour shadow chancellor; in cricket a bowler's deliveries are balls, and these spin from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliveries in cricket are balls, and these are a kind of spin delivery, so the plural matches with a question mark for example.

clue.text: Popular support up country

parts.note: something popular is 'in'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for support is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Popular backing for a rural region going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nation of South Asia, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Good English post is months in development

parts.note: a post is a station, a place where one is stationed

explanation.surface: A good English job taking months to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is a period of development lasting months, the time a baby grows before birth.

clue.text: They housed everyone briefly, during 4

parts.note: every person spent a short time inside a womb during pregnancy, the answer at 4

explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to GESTATION, so the clue reads: they housed everyone briefly, during gestation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs hold every one of us for the nine months of pregnancy, a short stay in a lifetime.

clue.text: Court that let loose a killer

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A court that set free a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' scrambles COURT THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer who slits throats; the word also describes ruthless people generally.

clue.text: Lead possibly given by beginner after team change

indicators.note: the beginner's letter is placed after the rearranged team
the letters of team are changed into a new order

parts.note: L stands for learner, a beginner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A team change after which a novice is given the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the team, and 'after' puts the learner's letter behind it. 'Lead' looks like a verb or a front position, but is the heavy element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a heavy element of this class, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: No way drink is an answer to all problems

parts.note: taken as written
ST, street, is a way
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Insisting that drink is no way to solve all your problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack cure-all or panacea, a remedy claimed to fix everything.

clue.text: Dances organised by weird bachelors

parts.note: rum means odd or weird in British slang
BAs are Bachelors of Arts

explanation.surface: Dances arranged by some strange single men.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old-fashioned British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballroom dances of Cuban origin, so examples of dances.

clue.text: Advised to be terribly rude but good-hearted

indicators.note: good-hearted puts the good letter in the heart of the jumbled word
done terribly, the letters of rude are jumbled

explanation.surface: Told to be dreadfully rude yet kind at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns RUDE into URED; '-hearted' puts G into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be urged is to be strongly encouraged or recommended to act, past tense like the clue.

clue.text: Watches what birds do, mostly, in the US

indicators.note: the shortened bird word goes inside the word for the US

parts.note: the States is the US

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: birds peck at their food

explanation.surface: Observes birds' habits, much as Americans might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter of the pecking word, and 'in' sets what is left just after the opening S of the American word.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch an event as an onlooker, a spectator, rather than taking part.

clue.text: Major article on public houses

indicators.note: in an across clue the article is placed on, after, the bars

parts.note: a bar is a public house, and two of them are needed
a bar is a public house, and two of them are needed
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A major piece writing about pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' is not an adjective: Major Barbara is a play by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shaw's play the title character is a Salvation Army major with this first name.

clue.text: Could be a life-saver for one trying to 17

definitions.text: Could be a life-saver for one trying to 17

parts.words: Could be a life-saver for one trying to 17
parts.note: 17 is the answer meaning to draw air into the lungs; an asthma sufferer struggling for breath relies on this device

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is BREATHE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma sufferers use a puffer device that delivers medicine to the lungs, often saving lives in an attack.

clue.text: Mob invading starts war, maybe

indicators.note: the answer invades, sits inside, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A rioting crowd's invasion sparks a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across startS WAR Maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarming crowd of people is a mob, a throng moving en masse.

clue.text: Party policy that's clear — on nothing at all!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: manifest means obvious or clear
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A party platform that's transparent, yet says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's published statement of its programme before an election.

clue.text: Out of stock, for example, come spring

definitions.text: Out of stock, for example, come spring

parts.words: Out of stock, for example, come spring
parts.note: stock is a garden flower, and 'out' means flowering, which it is in springtime

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of stock' reads as sold out, but stock here is the garden flower, and out means blooming.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out in spring are blooming, carrying open flowers on the stem.

clue.text: Inspire the brain with Ecstasy? Outrageous!

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wildness, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Feeding the brain ecstasy to inspire it is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspire' is used in its literal sense of drawing air in.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, inspiration means drawing air into the lungs, the opposite of expiration.

clue.text: Second bloomer overwhelms Pym, or M?

indicators.note: the second-plus-flower combination engulfs the name, which ends up inside it

parts.note: an aster is a flower, something that blooms
taken as written; Pym is a character name in le Carré's A Perfect Spy

explanation.surface: A floral blunder swamping a man named Pym, or someone called M.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: M runs British intelligence in Bond, so the character is an example of the chief of spies.

clue.text: A headless horse in NT becomes a worn-out nag

indicators.note: the pooled letters become a new arrangement
the horse word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A beheaded horse in the National Theatre turns into an exhausted old hack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' leaves ORSE; with A, IN and NT these letters are rearranged. Rocinante is Don Quixote's bony horse, whose name came to mean any decrepit nag.
explanation.definitionFit: The skinny steed of Don Quixote gave its name to any broken-down old horse.

clue.text: Recovers from a series of strokes

definitions.meaning: regains strength or health, picking up
in tennis, a prolonged exchange of shots; the answer is plural while this phrase is a single exchange

explanation.surface: Someone regains health after several medical strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick patient picks up again, and in racket games a long exchange of shots between players also takes this name.

clue.text: Go with bursting heart to lovers' meeting

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the heart of the word bursting is its two centre letters

explanation.surface: Arriving at a romantic rendezvous with a heart fit to burst.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic appointment between lovers is a rendezvous, an assignation.

clue.text: Get through the first set?

parts.note: babies cut their milk teeth, the first set, coming through the gums

explanation.walkthrough: 'first set' sounds like tennis; it is a baby's first teeth breaking through.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants cut their milk teeth, which push through the gums as the earliest set they grow.

clue.text: It was a match for Satan

definitions.meaning: an old brand name for a friction match struck to light fires
the Devil, the fallen angel's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'a match for' looks like an equal; the clue splits into an old kind of match and the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian friction match bore the name of the fallen angel, who is also called Satan.

clue.text: Kind of seizure grips the ring, causing nasty cough

indicators.note: the seizure word holds the letter within it

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power
R is taken here for ring, as in the boxing ring

explanation.surface: A spasm in the boxing ring triggering a horrible cough.
explanation.definitionFit: A childhood infection of the airways marked by a harsh barking cough.

clue.text: Overnight stay, sheltering ducks, appropriately

parts.note: birds settle on a perch for the night, and the word has two Os, cricket ducks, inside

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so 'ducks' are Os, and the word does shelter two Os, hence 'appropriately'.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle to sleep for the night, so a place for an overnight stay.

clue.text: After tasting, tucked in with a will

indicators.note: the eating word comes after the trial word

parts.note: a tasting is a test or trial of food or wine
to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in is ate

explanation.surface: Eating heartily after sampling, with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' looks like 'enthusiastically'; it is the legal sense, having left a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies leaving a valid legal will is said to die in that state.

clue.text: Reverse roles as a form of punishment

indicators.note: reverse means the word for roles is read backwards

parts.note: acting roles are parts

explanation.surface: Swapping roles as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather band used for beating, once a common school punishment.

clue.text: Press take jumbled notes to be a source of 7

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: jumbled says the letters of notes are mixed up

explanation.surface: Pressing, then shuffling notes, to be the source of some lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbled' turns NOTES into STONE; 7 is METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock from which iron is extracted, an ore and so a source of metal.

clue.text: Gag made by some poor devil, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken, its silent W lost

parts.note: a wretch is some poor unfortunate person

explanation.surface: A joke told by an unfortunate fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but means to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to make the throat's spasm of vomiting without bringing anything up.

clue.text: A pillar of the theatre, perhaps, in a minor role

definitions.text: A pillar of the theatre, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a pillar in a playhouse is a load-bearing component of the building
a secondary role in a play or film, below the lead

explanation.surface: A stalwart of the stage reduced to a bit-part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is not the lead plays a secondary role; a pillar is literally a structural element that holds up the building.
